We are looking for a Senior Manager, 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting to join our Accounting team. You will own revenue recognition, month-end close and reporting for Claude sold through our cloud service provider (CSP) channels: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. These channels are among the fastest-growing revenue streams at the company. They run on consumption-based, partner-reported data that changes every month.

You will be the accounting point of contact for the finance and partner teams at AWS, Google and Microsoft. Internally, you will partner with Finance, FAB, Engineering and business teams to turn partner billing feeds into accurate, auditable revenue. You will also lead the automation of a close that is still heavily manual. If you want to build the financial infrastructure behind a fast-growing AI company, come join us in our mission to build safe, beneficial AI.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the revenue close for cloud service provider Marketplace within a listed company timeline.

  • Prepare and review revenue, revenue-share, reserve journal entries, accruals and true-ups including memos for accounting assessments and judgments.

  • Own balance sheet reconciliations, reserves, and the usage-to-invoice-to-cash bridge.

  • Perform monthly and quarterly flux analysis and prepare flux decks for leadership.

  • Own quarter-end deliverables, including footnote disclosures, flux commentary and presentations to leadership and Corporate Accounting.

  • Serve as the primary contact for external auditors.

  • Review the work of accountants and contractors, set the close calendar, and keep close packages complete and audit-ready.

  • Own monthly and quarterly 3P revenue reporting for leadership and FP&A, by partner, model, product, region and customer.

  • Review partner usage, invoice, disbursement and fraud reports each month, and resolve data issues before close.

  • Serve as the accounting point of contact for the finance, engineering and product teams and drive reporting improvements that support an on-time close.

  • Apply ASC 606 to 3P arrangements, including principal-vs-agent, variable consideration and reseller arrangements.

  • Estimate and document reserves, including credit loss (ASC 326).

  • Assess the accounting for new 3P products, programs and billing changes, partnering with Technical Accounting on complex judgments.

  • Partner with the Engineering teams to automate manual close processes, including SQL-driven workbooks, automated reconciliations and system-generated journal entries.

  • Own 3P SOX controls, including design, documentation, gap remediation and audit evidence.

  • Partner with FP&A, Treasury, AR and business teams on forecasts, cash and partner disputes.

Minimum qualifications

  • Have strong ASC 606 knowledge, especially principal-vs-agent, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, and consumption-based revenue.

  • Have owned a month-end close with tight deadlines and reviewed journal entries, reconciliations and flux analysis.

  • Have built revenue reporting from large, imperfect third-party data sets and reconciled it to the general ledger.

  • Have managed external partner relationships where you depended on their data, and pushed for fixes.

  • Have strong SQL skills (BigQuery or similar) and experience automating close workbooks or reconciliations.

  • Have designed or operated SOX controls and supported external audits.

  • Communicate clearly with accounting, finance, business and engineering teams.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built.

Preferred qualifications

  • Have 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 3+ years managing revenue accounting or close teams.

  • A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent (ACA, ACCA).

  • Big 4 audit experience combined with industry experience at a high-growth tech or SaaS company.

  • Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller or channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace).

  • Experience with usage-based and subscription revenue models.

  • Hands-on experience with Workday Financials, NetSuite, Numeric, Hex or similar close and reporting tools.

  • Experience with IPO readiness.

  • Experience using AI tools to automate accounting and reporting work.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Anthropic runs one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry, across multiple accelerator families, CPU families, clouds, neoclouds, and on-prem sites. Capacity Engineering owns the data, tooling, and systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization of that fleet: we partner on supply deals, wire telemetry from day zero, own the canonical capacity data layer, and build the planning and enforcement tools every research and product team relies on. This role sits in the Planning pillar, on the Demand Planning team, and works daily with research engineering, pretraining, inference, compute supply, finance, and external vendors.

You own the tranches. The job has two halves that feed each other. Upstream, you take the Demand Planning forecast and turn it into per-tranche requirements — shape, interconnect, region, supporting resources, date — and carry those into sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews so we contract for capacity we can actually use when we need it. Downstream, you own the integrated schedule and system of record for every tranche in flight — from contracted through reserved, ingested, in-cluster, healthy, and occupied — and you drive the owners of each hop to their dates. Every slip you see downstream becomes a contract-language fix, an automation, or a correction fed back to the forecast.

What you'll do

  • Turn the forecast into per-tranche requirements. Take the Demand Planning forecast plus direct input from research, pretraining, and inference planners, and convert it into concrete accelerator, interconnect, region, supporting-resource, and date requirements for each tranche. Represent those in sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews, including which contractual terms actually move delivery dates.
  • Qualify tranches for deliverability before signature. The Capacity Planner signs fit-to-forecast; you sign whether the shape can land schedulable, healthy, and instrumented in that region on that date, with storage, egress, identity in place.
  • Close the delivery loop. Track forecast-versus-delivered on shape, region, and timing for every tranche; publish the variance; and feed it back to Demand Planning and into the next contract.
  • Own the bring-up system of record. Define the canonical contract-to-occupied state machine with explicit entry and exit criteria per stage, and make it a first-class object in the capacity data layer so every downstream tool sees in-flight capacity, not only what has landed.
  • Run a portfolio of bring-ups in parallel — new cloud regions, on-prem sites, neocloud blocks — with one integrated schedule spanning provider milestones, cluster creation, network turn-up, storage readiness, health burn-in, and first-workload landing. 
  • Drive readiness automation: All capacity systems are fully integrated for all new capacity, from contracted through ingested, automated and scaled.
  • Instrument and publish the numbers that matter — time-to-occupied and paid-idle dollars per tranche — with executive-level reporting on status, tradeoffs, and risk across the portfolio.

What you bring

  • Significant experience delivering large-scale infrastructure — cloud regions, accelerator clusters, HPC systems, or bare-metal fleets — at multi-region scale or ≥10k accelerators (or CPU/storage equivalent).
  • Technical range from through cluster orchestration and node health, up to the telemetry and planning tables on top — enough to debug where they disagree rather than route it.
  • SQL and enough Python to answer your own questions and build your own reporting.
  • A degree in a technical field or an equivalent engineering track record.

Preferred

  • Reserved-capacity onboarding, private offers, or capacity commitments with cloud or neocloud providers.
  • Enough demand-planning exposure to challenge a forecast, translate it into per-tranche requirements, and feed delivery variance back into it.
  • Data center or colocation delivery: power and space planning, network turn-up, site acceptance, vendor management.
  • Accelerator health and burn-in, collective-communications sanity testing, or fleet-health SLOs — and a rigorous definition of "healthy."
  • Systems of record or lifecycle services for infrastructure assets.
  • Onboarding a new hardware generation into an existing scheduler and observability stack.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Applications are now open for our January cohort - apply here by October 30.

Anthropic Fellows Program overview

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on an empirical project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.

What to expect

  • 4 months of full-time research 
  • Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers 
  • Access to a shared workspace (in either Bay Area, California, Toronto, Canada, or London, UK)
  • Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community
  • Weekly stipend of 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR + benefits (these vary by country)
  • Funding for compute (~$15k/month) and other research expenses

Interview process

The interview process will include an initial application & reference check, technical assessments & interviews, and a research discussion. 

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Compensation

The expected base stipend for this role is 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension).

Across the workstreams, you may be a good fit if you:

  • Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole
  • Are excited to transition into empirical AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic
  • Have a strong technical background in computer science, mathematics, or physics
  • Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments
  • Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Strong candidates may also have:

  • Strong background in a discipline relevant to a specific Fellows workstream (e.g. economics, social sciences, or cybersecurity)
  • Experience in areas of research or engineering related to their workstream

Candidates must be:

  • Fluent in Python programming
  • Available to work full-time on the Fellows program

AI Safety Fellows

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include:

  • Sam Bowman
  • Sara Price
  • Alex Tamkin
  • Nina Panickssery
  • Trenton Bricken
  • Logan Graham
  • Jascha Sohl-Dickstein
  • Joe Benton
  • Collin Burns
  • Fabien Roger
  • Samuel Marks
  • Kyle Fish
  • Ethan Perez

Our mentors will lead projects in select AI safety research areas, such as:

  • Scalable Oversight: Developing techniques to keep highly capable models helpful and honest, even as they surpass human-level intelligence in various domains.
  • Adversarial Robustness and AI Control: Creating methods to ensure advanced AI systems remain safe and harmless in unfamiliar or adversarial scenarios.
  • Model Organisms: Creating model organisms of misalignment to improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise.
  • Model Internals / Mechanistic Interpretability: Advancing our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures.
  • AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations.

On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about past projects, including:

  • Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data: Alex Cloud and Minh Le, et al., mentors including Samuel Marks and Owain Evans
  • Open-source circuits: Michael Hanna and Mateusz Piotrowski with mentorship from Emmanuel Ameisen and Jack Lindsey

For a full list of representative projects for each area, please see these blog posts: Introducing the Anthropic Fellows Program for AI Safety Research, Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions.

Unique candidate criteria

You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:

  • Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems
  • Have experience with empirical ML research projects
  • Have experience working with large language models
  • Have experience in one of the research areas mentioned above
  • Have a track record of open-source contributions

AI Security Fellows

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include:

  • Nicholas Carlini
  • Keri Warr
  • Evyatar Ben Asher
  • Keane Lucas
  • Newton Cheng

On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about some past Fellows projects, including:

  • AI agents find $4.6M in blockchain smart contract exploits: Winnie Xiao and Cole Killian, mentored by Nicholas Carlini and Alwin Peng
  • Strengthening Red Teams: A Modular Scaffold for Control Evaluations: Chloe Loughridge et al., mentored by Jon Kutasov and Joe Benton

Unique candidate criteria

You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:

  • Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems
  • Have contributed to open-source projects in LLM- or security-adjacent repositories
  • Have demonstrated success in bringing clarity and ownership to ambiguous technical problems
  • Have experience with pentesting, vulnerability research, or other offensive security work
  • Have a demonstrated willingness to do the "dirty work" that produces high-quality outputs
  • Have reported CVEs or been awarded bug bounties
  • Have experience with empirical ML research projects
  • Have experience with deep learning frameworks and experiment management

Logistics

Logistics Requirements: To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program.

Workspace Locations: We have designated shared workspaces in London and Berkeley where fellows will work from and mentors will visit. We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada. We will ask you about your availability to work from Berkeley or London (full- or part-time) during the program.

Visa Sponsorship: We are not currently able to sponsor visas for fellows. To participate in the Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the UK, the US, or Canada.

Program Duration: The program runs for 4 months, full-time. If you can't commit to the full duration, please still apply and note your constraints in the application. We review these requests on a case-by-case basis.

Please note: We do not guarantee that we will make any full-time offers to fellows. However, strong performance during the program may indicate that a Fellow would be a good fit for full-time roles at Anthropic. In previous cohorts, 25-50% of fellows received a full-time offer, and we’ve supported many more to go on to do great work on AI safety and security at other organizations.

Applications and interviews are managed by Constellation, our recruiting and program partner.   • Run executive briefings, technical workshops, and enablement sessions for both leadership and engineering audiences

  • 6+ years of experience as a Software Engineer, Solutions Architect, Forward Deployed Engineer, or technical founder
  • Experience in a pre-sales or technical advisory role selling into large enterprises, ideally in the French market, including scoping and designing complex solutions
  • Experience with value-based selling, meaning you can build a business case, quantify impact, and present it to senior decision makers
  • Comfort presenting to, and building relationships with, C-level and VP-level stakeholders
  • Experience owning the technical win in enterprise deals: evaluations, proofs of concept and technical due diligence with engineering, security, legal and procurement teams

  • A hands-on engineering background, including building and deploying production applications, so you can relate to engineering leaders and their teams
  • Familiarity with enterprise security, compliance, and architecture requirements, and experience working through them with customer teams
  • The ability to explain complex AI concepts clearly to both technical and executive audiences, and to move between industries such as financial services, healthcare, retail, and manufacturing
  • A passion for making powerful technology safe and beneficial

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As an Applied AI Engineer on the Startups team at Anthropic, you will be a trusted technical advisor to the top AI-native life sciences and biotech startups as they grow from early product to scale. Some of these companies build products on Claude that they sell to the rest of the industry, and others do the science themselves and want Claude woven into how their own research runs, and this role works with both. You'll lead deep technical engagements, partnering directly with startup engineering and scientific teams to help them build their products on Claude and run their own research with it, advising on implementation and agent design as they build what is newly possible with AI in the life sciences. You will bridge the gap between what Claude can do and what the life sciences need, working alongside some of the strongest teams in the field on problems that matter and pushing the boundaries of AI in science as you go.

Working closely with Applied AI Architects, Account Executives, and Anthropic's Product, Engineering, and Research teams, you'll help startups build at the edge of what is possible with Claude. You'll leverage your AI engineering expertise and your scientific domain knowledge to develop custom evaluation frameworks, design scalable architectures, and create the technical resources that enable life sciences startups to succeed with Claude.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as a deep technical advisor to high-potential life sciences and biotech startups, whether Claude sits inside the product they sell or inside the way they make discoveries, working alongside them to build innovative use cases that push the boundaries of AI in scientific research and development

  • Work hands-on with startup engineering teams and their scientists through pair programming and architecture reviews that accelerate their development, and understand their scientific workflows end to end so that your guidance fits into real research pipelines

  • Develop prototypes and technical documentation, including evaluation suites, scientifically grounded benchmarks, AI engineering techniques, and architecture diagrams, that enable startups to build, operate, and scale with Claude

  • Create reference implementations and sample code that many companies can adopt without starting from scratch, such as example MCP servers for domain-specific data sources like genomics platforms, literature databases, and experimental repositories, along with agent skills for common scientific workflows

  • Collaborate closely with Applied AI Architects to maintain context and continuity across customer engagements

  • Identify patterns across engagements, including what is hard about deploying AI in the life sciences such as heterogeneous data, auditability requirements, and the gap between a working prototype and a system that scientists trust, and contribute insights back to Product, Engineering, Research, and the broader Applied AI team, including feedback on the model capabilities and product features that would most accelerate discovery work

  • Create technical content for startup audiences including documentation, tutorials, and sample code

  • Represent Anthropic across the life sciences startup ecosystem and foster community engagement through hackathons, webinars, technical office hours, in-person founder events, and research show and tells

  • Travel to customer sites for workshops, implementation guidance, and relationship building

You may be a good fit if you have

  • Deep experience in the life sciences or biotech, gained through research or industry work in areas such as genomics, drug discovery, molecular design, lab automation, or clinical development, along with strong opinions of your own about how to bridge the gap between what AI can do today and what the life sciences need

  • 4+ years of technical experience as a software engineer, ML or research engineer, computational biologist, research scientist, or technical founder, with either production experience building LLM-powered applications, including prompting, context engineering, agent architectures, evaluation frameworks, and deployment at scale, or a track record of successfully applying AI to real scientific work in the lab or in research

  • Experience with startups or high-growth companies and a love of working with founders and small teams that move quickly

  • Strong technical communication skills, with the ability to translate complex AI concepts into architectural decisions and actionable implementation plans for both engineering and scientific audiences and to run technical workshops, hackathons, or developer-focused events

  • A collaborative approach to working across teams, the ability to context-switch across scientific domains and use cases, and a passion for making powerful technology safe and beneficial

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$280,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As Anthropic's Data Center Security Operations Lead , you will own day-to-day physical security operations across our data center campuses in the area, including sites run with operating partners. You will be the person on the ground: the one who knows each site, its guard force, its local responders and what is actually happening on the floor.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with no direct reports. You'll be on-site most weeks and get things done through people and companies you don't manage: site operators, guard vendors, construction and infrastructure partners, and your colleagues on the Data Center Security Engineering team. You will have the authority to make operational calls at your sites, and you'll work with the team's systems and delivery roles to take over each new site as it moves into operation.

The function is still in build mode. The work is ambiguous and changes as strategy changes. We need someone who can scope a loosely defined problem, carry it through to a result without waiting for a mature playbook, and treat security as an enabler of business outcomes.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the physical security operations program across our North East campuses, from a site's move into operations through steady state

  • Act as first call for site issues, including after hours, leading incident response and investigations and writing up what happened and what changes

  • Own guard force and vendor performance: post coverage, attrition, SLA grading, and the conversations that follow

  • Make time-sensitive operational and escalation decisions at your sites

  • Adapt company-wide standards into post orders, patrol standards, and badging and visitor procedures, keeping them consistent across sites and flagging where a standard doesn't fit

  • Partner with build, delivery and engineering teams on design and activation so that each turnover to operations is clean

  • Build and keep local relationships with law enforcement, emergency services, landlords and site operators

  • Lead cross-functional security work and represent your sites in infrastructure, compute and real estate decisions

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. You'll be the engineer who owns autonomous systems across that footprint as one security domain, from both sides: drones, ground robots and automated vehicles for patrol, inspection and moving hardware, including the security of that automation inside secure areas, and the detection systems that tell us what is flying over or operating near a site uninvited.

You set the approach, select and integrate the platforms and sensors, write the requirements vendors build to, and run what you ship, from the operating model where operators assign missions and machines carry them out to the playbook that turns a detection into an identified track and a well-evidenced handoff to whoever holds authority over the airspace. Interdiction is not part of this role. The goal is security that runs itself: coverage, fleet health and evidence verified continuously, with tools and AI agents doing the routine triage. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well.

You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including its physical security systems engineers and the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's data center operations and legal teams, and directly with site operators, equipment vendors and aviation and public safety authorities. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure.

Key responsibilities

  • Autonomous security and inspection systems: own the drones, ground robots and other autonomous platforms for perimeter patrol, incident response and infrastructure inspection: platform selection, operating model, operator qualification, maintenance, and the data path from machine to analyst

  • Security of site automation: engineer the controls on automated vehicles, robots and similar machines that move hardware or work inside secure areas: identity and access, network isolation, what they may record and where it goes, fail-secure behavior, their place in chain of custody, and acceptance before they enter a site

  • Regulatory and site constraints: establish what we may sense, fly, drive, record and retain at each site, partner-operated sites included, under the aviation, spectrum, privacy and safety rules that apply there, with the waivers and approvals that extend it and coordination with local authorities set up before it is needed

  • Health monitoring: define and test heartbeats, loss-of-coverage and lost-link alarms and fail-secure behavior, so a silent sensor or machine shows as a fault, not a quiet day

  • Vendor requirements and acceptance: write the requirements, evaluate against live flights and runs, and hold vendors to what they ship

Minimum qualifications

  • Have engineered autonomous or sensing systems in the field (drones, ground robots, automated vehicles, or RF, radar or optical detection sensors): selected, integrated or secured them for an operation other people relied on, and verified what they actually do against real targets or runs rather than a datasheet

  • Have integrated systems you did not build (vendor APIs, SDKs, appliances, machine and sensor telemetry) into a platform that outlives any one of them

  • Read and review code, design the data systems behind security tooling, and build automation (often with AI coding agents) using Git and code review

  • Have done this work hands-on for data centers, critical infrastructure or a large hardware fleet

  • Experience with counter-drone (counter-UAS) detection, airspace surveillance or air traffic data systems

  • Experience running a robot, drone or automated-vehicle fleet in an industrial, logistics or data center setting: fleet management, mission planning, safety cases

  • Experience with physical security operations at large sites, with law enforcement or aviation authorities, or at sites you did not fully control: cloud, colocation or GPU cloud operators

  • Communicate status, risk, and resolution to non-technical stakeholders in clear, calm, jargon-free language
  • Handle confidentiality and access requirements for sensitive sessions, including recording and streaming controls

Event Intake, Scoping & Scheduling

  • Own the event technology intake process end-to-end: request triage, technical scoping conversations, and staffing
  • Right-size production approach to event type, translating stakeholder goals into an equipment and staffing plan that fits the constraints and scope of our team’s SLA
  • Take on genuinely novel events and leave a repeatable standard behind — a template, runbook, or gear list that makes the next one easier than the first and repeatable by the team
  • Maintain the event technology calendar and coordinate coverage across the AV Operations team
  • Partner with Events, Internal Communications, and Workplace teams on lead times, expectations, and readiness

Support Operations & Room Health

  • Execute preventative maintenance programs and recurring room sweeps across event spaces and conference rooms
  • Maintain and test inventory of equipment including wireless microphones, cameras, and portable production gear pre event, following event production framework
  • Contribute to runbooks, standard operating procedures, and knowledge base documentation
  • Surface recurring operational pain points to AV Engineering as candidates for systemic fixes

You May Be a Good Fit If You:

  • Have 8+ years of hands-on experience in AV operations, live event production, or technical event support
  • Have owned the technical side of live productions end-to-end — not just operated a single position
  • Bring working fluency across event audio, video, camera, and streaming systems, with enough depth to diagnose problems rather than only report them
  • Are energized rather than drained by being the front-facing technical partner to executives and event producers
  • Bring structure to ambiguity by building systems for repeatable events

Strong Candidates May Also Have:

  • Technical direction for corporate broadcasts, conferences, or multi-camera productions
  • Q-SYS DSP platform, including reading and reasoning about existing audio/video routing and control designs
  • PTZ and professional camera systems, camera control units, and multi-camera workflows
  • Video conferencing platforms and hardware including Google Meet, Zoom Rooms, and hybrid meeting technologies
  • Live streaming workflows including encoders and encoding settings, contribution and delivery protocols (RTMP, SRT, HLS)
  • Network fundamentals for AV-over-IP including multicast, VLANs, QoS, and bandwidth management
  • Ticketing and workflow systems such as Jira, and building intake or request workflows within them
  • Coordinating AV contractors, integrators, and labor for event coverage

  • This role will be based in our San Francisco HQ
  • This role is expected to be in office 5 days per week
  • Occasional evening and early-morning coverage is expected around major events
  • 4-6 weeks of travel annually will be expected for this role for distributed event support as needed

We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is seeking a partnerships leader to own the tri-party motion for systems integrator partnerships selling through AWS. Global systems integrators and specialist SIs are how Claude reaches enterprise customers at scale, and AWS is the surface most of that work runs on. You will own the intersection of those two ecosystems.

In this role, you will build the go-to-market motion that turns partner interest into joint pipeline and closed revenue, working across AWS's partner organization and the AWS practices inside the world's largest integrators. You will define how Claude is positioned inside AWS partner programs, design the commercial mechanics that let partners transact and get rewarded, and build the joint plays that partners take to their customers.

This is a build role. The partner ecosystem is early, the programs are still being designed, and you will be operating across three organizations whose incentives on any given deal don’t always line up. You will help shape how frontier AI technology reaches the enterprise through the services ecosystem.

You will report directly to the Head of AWS GTM Partnerships.
